About Beamable 

Beamable is the backend and LiveOps infrastructure platform for game developers, the system that lets studios build, operate, and scale live games without constructing the underlying architecture themselves. Backend services, identity, analytics, meta-game systems, virtual economies, and AI-native tooling: all integrated into a single platform that eliminates the point-solution stitching that has defined game development for too long. Beamable also powers Wingman, an agentic LiveOps product that gives game teams a unified operating system to understand, optimize, and act on live game performance in real time. This is the future of how games are operated.

Beamable is part of FIRY, a founder-led global technology portfolio operating at the intersection of gaming, AI-powered performance marketing, and developer infrastructure. Acquired in January 2026, and together with Skillz, our competition platform, and RZR, our AI-driven ad network, Beamable sits at the foundation of a compounding ecosystem that no standalone competitor can replicate. If you want to build the infrastructure that games run on at a company with the vision and resources to back it — Beamable is the right place to do it.

About the Role 

Beamable is seeking a Head of Product to shape its platform vision and lead its next phase of growth in the game backend market. This is an opportunity to build the product function from the ground up, guide the platform from early access through public release, and advance AI integration to deliver meaningful value for game studios.

As the company’s senior product leader and sole product practitioner, you will own product strategy, roadmap, launch milestones, and success metrics, combining strategic direction with hands-on execution. You will work directly with studios and design partners, represent Beamable’s product vision at industry events, and translate customer insights into clear priorities. Success in this role means delivering a successful public launch, developing early-access studios into reference customers, and establishing a product foundation that drives adoption and sustained revenue growth.

Responsibilities 

  •  Product Strategy & Vision Ownership. Set the product vision for Beamable’s platform — spanning player engagement, developer tools, data enrichment, and player intelligence — and own the roadmap from early access through public release and beyond. Partner with the CRO on packaging, pricing, and tracking the studio funnel quantitatively.
  • Public Release & Launch Execution. Drive Beamable’s product through its launch milestones: early design partners, public release, and strategic partnerships. Define and own the go/no-go criteria for each milestone, ensuring the product ships when it’s ready to win.
  • Studio Partnership & Customer Discovery. Spend meaningful time every week with studios, design partners, and game developers — running discovery calls, demos, onboarding sessions, and roadmap reviews. Join sales calls and paid pilots with the CRO and turn each design partner into a reference case.
  • AI Integration & Product Intelligence. Define the guardrails, data policies, and feedback loops that make Beamable’s AI capabilities safe, effective, and trustworthy for game teams. Integrate with best-in-class tools studios already use and shape the intelligent systems that differentiate the platform.
  • Metrics Ownership & Product Function Build-Out. Define success metrics across the studio lifecycle — time to value, pilot conversion, retention, usage, and revenue per studio — and do your own analysis in SQL. Establish the product processes Beamable runs on: discovery, specs, prioritization, and launch reviews.
 
 

Key Competencies

  • Platform Product Strategy. Proven ability to set and execute product vision for a developer-facing platform, owning the strategy across multiple capability areas simultaneously — not just a feature set.
  • Customer-Facing Product Leadership. Equally credible with studio heads, producers, and engineers. Comfortable running a demo, leading a discovery call, supporting a sale, and representing the product at industry events including GDC and Gamescom.
  • Gaming Live-Ops Domain Expertise. Deep understanding of what a studio’s growth or live-ops team does day-to-day — events, offers, economies, segmentation, player support, and player data — and what slows them down.
  • AI/ML Product Judgment. Experience shipping AI or ML-driven features to production. Knows where AI adds genuine value, where it needs guardrails, and how to define data policies that serve both studio needs and platform integrity.
  • Data Fluency & Metrics Ownership. Can build dashboards, write SQL, and live with retention, churn, and revenue metrics over time. Runs experiments before big bets rather than after.
  • 0-to-1 Startup Product Leadership. Comfortable being the only PM in an ambiguous, fast-moving environment. Has built product processes from scratch and can hold the strategy and the execution at the same time.
  • Technical Depth. Conversant in data warehouses, APIs, SDKs, and system design. Can earn the respect of engineers and studio technical leads without needing a dedicated translator.

Experience 

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Business, Design, or a related field; equivalent experience considered.
  • 10+ years in product management, including experience as a product lead or head of product owning a product line’s strategy — not just a feature set.
  • Proven experience in gaming live-ops — either running live games or building tools for teams that do: events, offers, economies, segmentation, player support, or player data.

  • At least one AI or ML-driven feature shipped to production and used by real customers.

  • Experience with customer engagement platforms (Braze, CleverTap), game backends (PlayFab, Nakama, Unity Gaming Services), or data warehouses (Snowflake, BigQuery) preferred.
  • Experience taking a product from early access to public launch preferred.

Overview

Patchstack protects WordPress sites for hosts, agencies and developers, and we're now launching a security product for people building JavaScript apps with AI tools like Claude Code. That product is early. We have good signals from hosts and hackathons, but we haven't yet found who it serves best, what they value, or why they'll keep paying for it.

You'll be the product manager who finds that out. You'll talk to customers, use the product in real AI-assisted workflows, test ideas quickly with our designer and engineers, and build the measurement that tells us what's working. You'll work alongside two small engineering squads, a senior product designer, QA and infrastructure. You own which customer problems we invest in and how we learn from the results.

About you

You're happiest early, before the answers exist. You'd rather run a small test this week than wait for perfect data. You're comfortable in a terminal and have built things with AI-assisted tools, so you can use our product the way our customers do. You form your own view on technical claims rather than taking "it's not feasible" or "the metric improved" at face value. You say what you think, including when it's awkward, and you change your mind when the evidence says so. You work well in a flat team with little process, and you help people around you get better rather than taking work off them.

Responsibilities

jobs.title: Anthropic: Autonomous Systems Security Engineer
jobs.description:
Headquarters: Remote-Friendly (Travel Required) | San Francisco, CA

About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

Claude is trained and served on hardware in data centers Anthropic operates and in sites partners build and run for us. DCSE secures that footprint: the sites, the hardware moving through them, and the people and vendors who touch it. You'll be the engineer who owns autonomous systems across that footprint as one security domain, from both sides: drones, ground robots and automated vehicles for patrol, inspection and moving hardware, including the security of that automation inside secure areas, and the detection systems that tell us what is flying over or operating near a site uninvited.

You set the approach, select and integrate the platforms and sensors, write the requirements vendors build to, and run what you ship, from the operating model where operators assign missions and machines carry them out to the playbook that turns a detection into an identified track and a well-evidenced handoff to whoever holds authority over the airspace. Interdiction is not part of this role. The goal is security that runs itself: coverage, fleet health and evidence verified continuously, with tools and AI agents doing the routine triage. We favor simple, standard controls and tools that can be verified over elaborate ones. We use Claude throughout our engineering workflow and expect you to as well.

You'll work with the rest of DCSE, including its physical security systems engineers and the engineers on its security monitoring platform, with Anthropic's data center operations and legal teams, and directly with site operators, equipment vendors and aviation and public safety authorities. The role is based in San Francisco, with remote applicants in the US considered, and involves regular travel to data center sites, which are critical infrastructure.

Key responsibilities

  • Autonomous security and inspection systems: own the drones, ground robots and other autonomous platforms for perimeter patrol, incident response and infrastructure inspection: platform selection, operating model, operator qualification, maintenance, and the data path from machine to analyst

  • Tools, automation and AI agents: build the integrations that carry detections, tracks, telemetry and fleet health into the team's security monitoring platform, and the tools and agents that triage detections, check fleet health and assemble evidence. When a review keeps costing people time, you build the tool or agent that retires it

  • Detection of uncrewed systems: engineer the sensing that tells us what is flying over or operating near a site, what it is and who needs to know: sensor selection and evaluation against live targets, per-site coverage, classification and false-alarm handling, and the playbook from first detection to handoff, with evidence retained

  • Security of site automation: engineer the controls on automated vehicles, robots and similar machines that move hardware or work inside secure areas: identity and access, network isolation, what they may record and where it goes, fail-secure behavior, their place in chain of custody, and acceptance before they enter a site

  • Regulatory and site constraints: establish what we may sense, fly, drive, record and retain at each site, partner-operated sites included, under the aviation, spectrum, privacy and safety rules that apply there, with the waivers and approvals that extend it and coordination with local authorities set up before it is needed

  • Health monitoring: define and test heartbeats, loss-of-coverage and lost-link alarms and fail-secure behavior, so a silent sensor or machine shows as a fault, not a quiet day

  • Vendor requirements and acceptance: write the requirements, evaluate against live flights and runs, and hold vendors to what they ship

Minimum qualifications

  • Have engineered autonomous or sensing systems in the field (drones, ground robots, automated vehicles, or RF, radar or optical detection sensors): selected, integrated or secured them for an operation other people relied on, and verified what they actually do against real targets or runs rather than a datasheet

  • Have integrated systems you did not build (vendor APIs, SDKs, appliances, machine and sensor telemetry) into a platform that outlives any one of them

  • Read and review code, design the data systems behind security tooling, and build automation (often with AI coding agents) using Git and code review

  • Have done this work hands-on for data centers, critical infrastructure or a large hardware fleet

  • Have designed inside a regulatory or safety constraint (aviation, spectrum, privacy, machine safety or similar) and can show the decision it drove

  • Own a domain end to end: set the approach, carry it through with vendors, site operators, partners and authorities, and run it as something people depend on every day

Preferred qualifications

  • Remote pilot certification (for example FAA Part 107) and experience flying beyond visual line of sight under a waiver or exemption

  • Experience with counter-drone (counter-UAS) detection, airspace surveillance or air traffic data systems

  • Experience running a robot, drone or automated-vehicle fleet in an industrial, logistics or data center setting: fleet management, mission planning, safety cases

  • Experience securing embedded, operational technology or robotic systems: device identity, network segmentation, update control, logging

  • Experience with physical security operations at large sites, with law enforcement or aviation authorities, or at sites you did not fully control: cloud, colocation or GPU cloud operators

  • Have built AI agents or automation that replaced recurring manual work

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. 

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary:
$320,000—$405,000 USD

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed.  Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

jobs.title: Carrot: Sr. IT Systems Engineer
jobs.description:
Headquarters: Remote

About Carrot:

Carrot is the leading global fertility and family care platform, built on intelligent care orchestration: the right clinical guidance, at the right moment, in the context of each member’s life. More than a thousand multinational employers, health plans, and health systems trust Carrot to support millions of members across 195 countries – from pre-pregnancy through menopause and major life moments in between. Carrot's comprehensive clinical program delivers industry-leading cost savings for plan sponsors and award-winning experiences and improved outcomes for millions of people worldwide.

Carrot is widely regarded as a defining force in healthcare innovation as a recipient of several top-tier awards, including Fast Company's 'Most Innovative Companies' and CNBC's '100 Barrier Breaking Startups'. The company is regularly cited by leading global outlets — including The Economist, Bloomberg, The Wall Street Journal, NPR, ABC News, and Harvard Business Review — as a leading voice on digital health, the future of work, and family health. Learn more at get-carrot.com.

The Opportunity 

Carrot is looking for a Sr. IT Systems Engineer to design, scale, and secure the identity, endpoint, and SaaS platforms that power our global, remote-first workforce. You will set the technical direction for how employees and devices connect to Carrot systems, while staying hands-on in the tooling, automation, and complex problem-solving that make IT reliable at scale.

This role sits at the center of IT engineering. You will lead larger initiatives from design through rollout, partner closely with Information Security on zero-trust and compliance priorities, and raise the bar for the rest of the team through standards, documentation, and mentorship. If you want broad technical ownership, influence over the IT roadmap, and the chance to build systems that grow with a high-growth healthcare company, this role was built for that.

What You’ll Own

In this role, you will:

  • Architect and own Carrot's identity, endpoint, and SaaS platforms, including Okta, JAMF, Intune, and Google Workspace, with a focus on security, reliability, and user experience
  • Lead design and rollout of larger IT initiatives, such as zero-trust access models, device compliance frameworks, and global endpoint standards
  • Build and maintain automation and infrastructure as code that manage configuration, provisioning, and lifecycle workflows at scale
  • Partner with Information Security to design controls, drive vulnerability management, and keep Carrot audit-ready for SOC 2, HIPAA, and customer security reviews
  • Serve as the senior technical escalation point, leading incident response and root cause analysis for complex or high-impact issues
  • Define engineering standards, runbooks, and documentation, and mentor IT teammates to grow their technical depth
  • Evaluate vendors and tools, build business cases, and make clear recommendations on build versus buy tradeoffs
  • Design environments that support global care and operations teams, including secure and efficient remote computing setups
  • Contribute to the IT roadmap and communicate priorities, risks, and progress to technical and business stakeholders

What Success Looks Like  

In your first 12–18 months, you will have:

  • Established a clear, documented architecture and standards for identity, endpoint, and SaaS management that the team can build on
  • Delivered at least one major platform initiative, such as a zero-trust access model or endpoint modernization, with measurable gains in security posture and employee experience
  • Reduced manual IT work through automation and infrastructure as code, with a measurable drop in recurring ticket volume
  • Strengthened audit readiness, contributing to clean results on security and compliance reviews
  • Raised the technical capability of the team through mentorship, documentation, and shared standards
  • Built trusted partnerships with Information Security, People, Engineering, and Finance

About You

You likely have:

  • 6+ years of experience in IT systems engineering, endpoint engineering, or infrastructure roles, including ownership of production platforms
  • Deep, hands-on expertise with identity and access platforms such as Okta, including SSO, SCIM, lifecycle automation, and conditional access
  • Expert-level experience managing Mac and Windows fleets with JAMF and Intune, including packaging, deployment, security policy, and compliance enforcement
  • Strong scripting and automation skills (for example Python, Bash, or PowerShell), with experience using APIs and source-controlled configuration
  • Experience designing and implementing security controls, such as encryption, vulnerability management, and zero-trust principles, in partnership with Security teams
  • A track record of leading cross-functional technical projects from design through rollout without direct authority
  • Experience mentoring or technically guiding other engineers
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate complex tradeoffs for executive and non-technical audiences

Nice to Have ⭐

While not required, we would be especially excited if you bring:

  • Experience in healthcare, health tech, or another regulated environment (for example, HIPAA or SOC 2)
  • Experience with infrastructure as code and CI/CD practices applied to endpoint or SaaS configuration
  • Hands-on experience with AWS or GCP and modern cloud networking concepts
  • Experience designing remote computing environments for call center or clinical operations teams, such as VDI or managed browser models
  • Experience building AI-assisted workflows or tooling to improve IT operations
  • Relevant certifications (for example JAMF Certified Expert, Okta Certified Professional, or Microsoft Endpoint Administrator)

Why This Role Matters

Every Carrot employee depends on technology that is secure, reliable, and easy to use, whether they are supporting members through deeply personal care journeys or partnering with global employers. This role sets the technical foundation that makes that possible.

As Carrot continues to scale across geographies and functions, the architecture and standards you establish will protect member trust, strengthen our security posture, and give the business the speed and confidence to keep growing.

Why Candidates Join Carrot

Carrot offers the opportunity to do meaningful work in service of a deeply human mission.

Highlights include:

  • A mission-driven company focused on expanding access to fertility and family-forming care globally.
  • A high-growth environment where leaders are empowered to shape strategy and drive impact.
  • Competitive compensation, equity, and comprehensive benefits.
  • Flexible Time Off and a culture that actively encourages employees to recharge.
  • Comprehensive parental leave and family-forming benefits.
  • A collaborative, inclusive, and values-driven culture.
  • The opportunity to work alongside passionate, thoughtful teammates committed to improving healthcare outcomes worldwide.

 

Compensation

Carrot offers a holistic Total Rewards package designed to support our employees in all aspects of their lives inside and outside of work, including health and wellness benefits, retirement savings plans, short- and long-term incentives, parental leave, family-forming assistance, and a competitive compensation package.

  • Base Salary Range: $150,000 – $175,000 (primary range).
  • Geo-Tier Adjustment: Up to $190,000 for highly experienced candidates within 50 miles of San Francisco, NYC, or Seattle.

Actual compensation may vary from the posted base salary depending on your confirmed job-related skills and experience.

 

Fraud and Security Notice: Please note that all communication regarding job opportunities at Carrot will come exclusively from an @get-carrot.com email address. If you receive messages from any other domain, please disregard them and report the incident to: securityreporting@get-carrot.com

 

A Note on AI

At Carrot, we believe AI can help us work smarter, move faster, and create more meaningful experiences for our members, customers, and each other. While not every role requires deep technical AI expertise, we value people who are curious, eager to learn, and excited to thoughtfully incorporate AI into their day-to-day work.

For some roles, AI fluency is a core requirement—and we'll call that out clearly in the qualifications. For everyone else, we're looking for people who embrace new ways of working, use AI responsibly to improve quality and efficiency, and continue to learn as the technology evolves.

Why Carrot?

Carrot has received national and international recognition for its pioneering work, including Fast Company's Most Innovative Companies and World Changing Ideas, Inc. Power Partners, and Modern Healthcare’s Innovators. Carrot’s global workforce has been acknowledged with several accolades, including Fortune’s Best Workplaces in Healthcare, Great Place to Work, and Age-Friendly Employer certifications. Carrot is regularly featured in media reporting on issues related to the future of work, women in leadership, and healthcare innovation, including MSNBC, The Economist, Bloomberg, The Wall Street Journal, CNBC, National Public Radio, Harvard Business Review, and more. Learn more at carrotfertility.com.

jobs.title: Bybit: Blockchain Risk Control Lead
jobs.description:
Headquarters: Europe - Remote

About Us

Established in 2018, Bybit is one of the world’s leading cryptocurrency exchanges and digital financial platforms, serving over 80 million users across more than 200 countries and regions. Powered by world-class technology and a user-first mindset, Bybit delivers a seamless ecosystem across trading, payments, wealth management, custody, institutional services, and Web3 — connecting users to the future of digital finance.
 
Our core values define how we build. We listen, care and improve to create products and experiences that put users first. Backed by a global team of ambitious builders, problem-solvers, and innovators, we foster a high-performance and fast-moving environment where talent is empowered to drive real impact at the global scale. Supported by 24/7 multilingual customer service and a strong commitment to innovation, we are shaping the future of finance through technology, collaboration, and bold execution.
 
Today, Bybit is recognized as one of the most trusted and transparent platforms in the digital asset industry, continuing to expand its global presence while building the infrastructure for the next generation of financial services.

Job Brief

We are expanding our focus to cover AI-augmented threat intelligence and post-quantum cryptographic (PQC) security. The ideal candidate will combine deep blockchain forensics expertise with working knowledge of machine learning techniques for anomaly detection, and awareness of quantum computing threats to current cryptographic foundations (ECDSA, RSA) used across blockchain ecosystems. We value candidates who can bridge academia and industry and build collaborative relationships with research institutions to accelerate the adoption of emerging cryptographic and AI-driven techniques within the company.
 

Main Responsibilities of a Blockchain Risk Control Analyst/Researcher

Your main responsibilities will include:
  • Leveraging LLM techniques to drive the development of next-generation on-chain risk identification and threat intelligence systems, including autonomous agent workflows capable of continuous monitoring, self-triggered investigation, and automated operational responses — reducing manual intervention across the full risk lifecycle from detection to resolution;
  • Leading forensic investigations on real crypto theft, fraud, and market manipulation cases, integrating AI-assisted pattern recognition to accelerate root cause analysis;
  • Researching post-quantum cryptographic algorithms (NIST PQC: ML-KEM, ML-DSA, SLH-DSA, FALCON) and their implications for blockchain security; assessing quantum computing threats to existing cryptographic foundations (ECDSA secp256k1, hash functions) and evaluating migration paths;
  • Partnering with internal teams and external stakeholders for incident response, and engaging with academic institutions to translate frontier research into deployable security tools;
 

Key Requirements

  • You have a Master's or PhD's degree in Blockchain security, Computer Science, Data Science, or a related field.
  • You are good at programming languages commonly used in blockchain analytics (e.g., SQL, Python, Javascript)
  • Experience applying machine learning or AI techniques to blockchain data analysis, fraud detection, or threat intelligence
  • A strong publication record in top-level industry or academic conferences is highly valued.
  • You have experience with blockchain monitoring/forensic tools and analytics platforms.
  • Familiarity with NIST PQC standards (ML-KEM, ML-DSA, SLH-DSA, FALCON) and lattice/hash-based cryptography fundamentals is a plus;
  • Understanding of quantum computing threats to elliptic curve cryptography and implications for key management in Web3;
  • You have security or risk control experience as a plus.
  • You possess effective communication and collaboration abilities.
  • English is essential, and proficiency in Mandarin can be an advantage.

Why Join Us

Set minimum spend thresholds, monitor fatigue indicators, and deliver structured briefs to internal design and video teams for iterations, variations, and net-new creative concepts.

  • Data Visualization & Client Reporting: Build and manage Looker Studio dashboards demonstrating true acquisition ROI, downstream appointment volume, and sales conversion rates. Deliver structured weekly written updates detailing performance drivers, strategic shifts, and upcoming optimizations.
  • Conversion Rate Optimization & Funnel Operations: Audit full user journeys from click to qualification, proposing ongoing landing page enhancements. Execute technical SEO and Answer Engine Optimization (AEO) initiatives in coordination with senior leadership, including site speed fixes and email nurture workflows.
  • AI Workflow Integration: Leverage AI tools across daily operations, data analysis, reporting synthesis, and rapid creative ideation. Develop and document standard operating procedures that leverage AI to increase throughput without compromising quality or strategic rigor.

  • Downstream Conversion Focus: Demonstrated history driving high-intent B2C or high-consideration lead generation, measuring success by sales outcomes rather than raw lead volume.
  • Technical Infrastructure: Hands-on experience configuring GA4, GTM, Meta CAPI, offline conversion feeds, and custom Looker Studio dashboards.
  • Attribution Acumen: Solid understanding of multi-touch attribution, channel mix modeling constraints, and cross-platform reporting discrepancies.
  • AI Fluency: Active, daily integration of AI workflows into campaign development, copy iteration, or analytical operations.
  • Communication & Cadence: Exceptional written and verbal communication skills; ability to produce executive-ready client summaries and precise creative briefs.
  • Operational Alignment: Full availability to work aligned with Sydney, Australia (AEST/AEDT) business hours.
Preferred

jobs.title: Revenue Cycle Manager
jobs.description:
About Us

We are fixing US healthcare by building an AI-native physical care platform, starting with home health.

Home health is a $140B industry with less than $10B in EBITDA â 40% of revenue is spent on pure administrative waste. We automate this work with AI, creating a fundamentally different cost structure compared to incumbents. This lets us rapidly take market share by serving the 30% of patients who go untreated today.

By reshaping the cost structure of this industry, we unlock its growth.

We've built one of the best AI teams in the world (from Character AI, Scale, Palantir, Citadel, Jane Street) and paired them with a team of healthcare veterans to build a new type of healthcare company: one that delivers care at the speed of an AI company.

Our physical care platform already operates with 30pp higher gross margins than traditional home health providers. With our AI advantage, we pay nurses more, remove their admin burden, and unlock the scale economics that have been missing from this fragmented industry. If we served this entire $140B market, instead of $10B in EBITDA, we'd drive $60B.

We're starting with home health, then expanding to all delivered care. Our mission is "any care, any where".

Fundamentally, our incentives are aligned with America. Every dollar in revenue we make is two dollars taken out of the healthcare system. If we succeed, so does US healthcare.

Role overview

Weâre seeking a hands-on Revenue Cycle Management (RCM) Manager to lead and support a team of specialists in a home health environment. This manager will stay close to daily operations, monitor team performance, and respond quickly to questions and emerging issues to help the team meet its goals. The role focuses on accounts receivable (AR), helping the team move outstanding claims from follow-up to verified resolution.

What Youâll Do

  • Manage and support RCM specialists working across home health revenue cycle workflows.

  • Track attendance and monitor individual and team performance against established KPIs and daily quotas.

  • Review workflow boards throughout the day to spot backlogs, red flags, and specialists at risk of missing their end-of-day quotas.

  • Respond promptly to specialist questions while balancing real-time workflow monitoring and other team needs.

  • Identify process gaps and work with the team to resolve issues affecting daily performance.

  • Apply your home health and Homecare Homebase (HCHB) knowledge to help specialists navigate workflows and resolve operational questions.

Accounts receivable and collections

  • Guide specialists and team leads in prioritizing assigned commercial, Medicare, and Medicare Advantage receivables, including aged balances, payer responses, rejections, denials, and upcoming filing or appeal deadlines.

  • Oversee claim follow-up through resolution: verify claim status and payment, investigate collection barriers and underpayments, and guide appropriate corrections, reprocessing, reconsiderations, or appeals under payer-specific requirements.

  • Review and respond to escalations when a specialist cannot determine the next action; surface recurring payer, workflow, or system issues to leadership and coordinate their resolution.

  • Ensure claim activity, supporting evidence, next actions, and follow-up dates are documented accurately in the applicable AR workflow and HCHB.

  • Partner with billing, payment posting, prior authorization, clinical, and other teams to resolve discrepancies, obtain documentation, and follow paid-but-not-posted claims through resolution.

  • Review proposed write-offs for documented collection efforts and supporting evidence, and route them through the required approval and posting process.

Quality and team development

  • Review claim work for accurate denial interpretation, appropriate action, complete documentation, timely follow-up, and correct escalation; use findings to coach specialists and strengthen performance.

  • Support onboarding, payer and system cross-training, and regular knowledge sharing. Identify patterns behind collection challenges and update SOPs or workflows to prevent repeat issues.

  • Share frontline feedback on AR dashboards and automation with relevant teams to improve prioritization, visibility, and specialist workflows.

Basic Qualifications

  • Strong experience in home health revenue cycle operations.

  • Familiarity with Homecare Homebase (HCHB).

  • Experience managing RCM specialists, including tracking attendance and performance KPIs.

  • Experience monitoring workflows throughout the day and identifying risks to daily productivity targets.

  • Experience identifying collection challenges and implementing processes to resolve.

  • Working knowledge of AR follow-up, denial investigation, appeals or reprocessing, and payer-specific filing requirements.

  • Experience reviewing claim documentation and quality, escalating unresolved issues, and coordinating with billing or posting teams.

  • Ability to respond promptly to team questions while managing multiple priorities.

  • Ability to identify workflow or process gaps and help the team address them.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience managing distributed or offshore revenue cycle teams.

  • Familiarity with commercial fee-for-service and Medicare or Medicare Advantage home health claims, including episodic/PDGM workflows.

  • Experience with AR dashboards, clearinghouses, and payer portals such as Waystar and Availity.

  • Experience using denial trends, quality reviews, or operational data to improve collections workflows and team training.

What We Offer

  • Competitive salary

  • Comprehensive health insurance, dental, and commuter benefits

  • 401(k) retirement plan with employer contribution

  • Opportunity for growth in a fast-growing company

  • Collaborative team valuing innovation and problem-solving

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager
jobs.description:
About us

At Pencil, we are driving innovation in advertising technology through our state-of-the-art SaaS product, which harnesses Agentic AI to redefine content creation. Our mission is to make AI the default in advertising without replacing creative people. To achieve this, we need to make sure that our technology isn't just in the hands of big brands - we need to try to help small businesses and creative individuals too.

The role

Workflows are how most of the creative on Pencil gets made. A workflow is a visual sequence of steps, covering inputs, generation, brand assets, scoring, branching logic and delivery, that a person builds once and runs again whenever the job repeats, on demand or on a schedule. This role owns that product and the connections that feed it, with one goal: more workflows built and run, by more people, across every customer.

You will own Workflows and Integrations. That covers the workflow builder, templates, scheduling and run management, and the steps that workflows are built from. It also covers the platform's third-party connections outside media: digital asset management systems, file storage such as Google Drive, translation services, data services such as Foreplay, and more than a hundred other business tools. You will make those connections part of the workflow itself, so that a run can start from a client's systems and deliver back into them. You will build them on a common framework, so that each new connection is quicker to ship than the last and client teams can build on it for individual clients.

You will also own how workflows show up inside Scribble, our creative agent. Agents can already run as steps inside a workflow. The next step is for Scribble to find, build, change and run workflows on a person's behalf and report back as they run, and for a workflow to pause for a person's decision and act on it. You will work closely with the team that builds Scribble, and you will own the workflow experience it works through, so that a workflow behaves the same whether a person or an agent is driving it. When that works, building a workflow stops being a specialist job.

Key responsibilities

  • Own the charter for Workflows and Integrations: the durable problem, success metrics, and an explicit in and out scope list.

  • Grow adoption across every customer, measured by the number of workflows built and run and the number of people building them.

  • Make building a workflow simple enough for a marketer or creative to do without help, through templates, guided set-up and defaults that cover the common jobs.

  • Own the workflow experience that Scribble works through, so that an agent can find, build, change and run a workflow with the same tools a person uses.

  • Make human review part of the run: a workflow should pause for a person's decision, record it, and continue down the right path.

  • Make runs dependable at volume, with scheduling, run management, failure handling and clear status, so that a team trusts a workflow to run unattended.

  • Own third-party integrations outside media, from digital asset management and file storage to translation and data services, and make them built-in steps in a workflow, so that a run can start from a client's systems and deliver back into them.

  • Set the integration framework and standards that client teams build on when they connect a system for a single client.

  • Work with customers to find the jobs they repeat every week and turn them into workflows and templates that others can reuse.

  • Run the full lifecycle from discovery to post-launch review, with a written hypothesis before every ship and a review against it afterwards.

  • Use product data and structured customer feedback to set priorities, working backwards from evidenced customer need.

  • Partner closely with design on the builder experience, and with engineering on run reliability and the integration framework. Partner with the PMs who own Scribble, agents and the editor, and with the client teams who build on your framework.

Your background

You will have three to five years of product management experience, and you want to own a key product and take it to the next level. You might be a great fit if you can walk us through:

  • A product you grew from a small group of power users to broad adoption, and what you changed to get there.

  • Shipping a builder, automation or workflow tool, and what you learned about making something powerful easy to start with.

  • Building integrations with third-party platforms or APIs: how you chose which to build, and how you kept them working.

  • A time you built from validated customer need in a domain you had to go and learn. If your instinct is to start with a demo, this is not the role.

  • A decision you changed because the data told you to. Fluent in qual and quant.

  • Experience with AI agents or AI-assisted products is a plus.

You'll Thrive Here If Youâ¦

  • Move Fast. You're comfortable making decisions with imperfect information, iterating quickly, and fixing things before they become fires;

  • Stay Human. You care deeply about users and teammates, and design with empathy for real workflows;

  • Act Like an Owner. You take responsibility for outcomes, not just outputs. You spot problems early and take initiative to fix them.

  • Keep It Simple. You fight unnecessary complexity, design reusable patterns, and make hard things feel intuitive.

  • Love to Surprise. You enjoy finding unexpected ways to delight users, especially in the last mile of polish and usability.

KPIs & Success Measures

We will measure success through outcomes and quality, not just output:

  • Builder share (lead): percentage of monthly active users who build or edit a workflow. Target [TBD]%.

  • Workflow adoption (lead): percentage of monthly active users who run a workflow. Target [TBD]%.

  • Workflow run growth: month-on-month percentage growth in workflow runs. Target [TBD]%.

  • First workflow conversion: percentage of new users who complete a successful run within their first [TBD] days.

  • Share of generations through workflows: percentage of all generations produced by workflow runs.

  • Agent and human collaboration: percentage of workflow runs built or started by Scribble.

  • Connector adoption: percentage of active workspaces that use at least one third-party connection in a workflow each month. Target [TBD]%.

  • Integration usage: percentage of workflow runs that start from, or deliver to, a third-party connection. Target [TBD]%.

  • Reliability (hygiene bar): percentage of runs that complete without manual intervention, held at or above [TBD]%.

  • Learning velocity (supporting): percentage of launches reviewed after release against their stated hypothesis. Target 100%.

Benefits

  • 25 days PTO plus public holidays, although we operate a Flexible Time Off scheme

  • Health insurance / private medical cover

  • Monthly stipend towards wellness, fitness, and learning and development

  • Remote - work from anywhere in your home country

  • Enhanced parental leave policies, whether you become a parent through birth, adoption or surrogacy

  • Access to our Pencil office in The Shard, London for our UK employees

  • Flexible working hours

Deep Dive About Pencil

Pencil uses AI to make ads. Our mission is to make marketing effective and effortless. We want to become the default way ads get made - because AI ads are 10x faster and cheaper to make, and 2x better performing, than making them without AI.

We're called Pencil because we believe AI will be a tool for creative people, not a replacement - it may even be as fundamental a tool in the future as the pencil was in the past.

Pencil was founded in 2018 with a team from Google, Facebook and Uber with backing from Sequoia and Entrepreneur First. We were acquired by The Brandtech Group in 2023 to pursue a shared vision of bringing GenAI to the Fortune 500.

https://www.trypencil.com

About The Brandtech Group

The Brandtech Group's mission is to be the best company in the world at helping leading global brands drive growth by connecting content, data and media using technology.

It was founded in June 2015 (as You & Mr Jones) by former Havas Global CEO David Jones, with a simple mission to help brands do their marketing better, faster and cheaper using technology. It was renamed The Brandtech Group in January 2022.

Today it generates more than $1BN in revenue and is the largest global digital content partner for many of the world's biggest brands and companies, often using its unique in-housing model. It works with eight of the world's top 10 global advertisers and 49 of the world's top 100. Clients include Banco ItaÃº, Danone, Google, Intuit, LVMH, Microsoft, Morgan-Stanley, Netflix, Reckitt, Renault-Nissan, PayPal, TikTok, Uber and Unilever.

In addition, the Group invests in cutting-edge technology companies relevant to and with potential in marketing and has been investing in the AI, AR and the metaverse space since 2015. The Group was the first external investor in Niantic (creators of PokÃ©mon Go), alongside investments in AI Foundation (AI digital twins, personalized AI, and deep-fake detection 2018), Automat (AI chatbots, 2016), Elsy (AI media planning, 2016), Jivox (dynamic automated content, 2016), Crossing Minds (deep learning AI recommendation system, 2017), CreativeX (AI-driven content optimization, 2022), Zappar (AR, 2017), Provenance (blockchain, 2022) and GGP (the world's largest gaming fund).

The Group is one of the most prominent marketing industry voices on the prediction and movement to AI-driven marketing, including Generative AI. It was named one of the World's Most Innovative Companies 2021 by Fast Company, and by CB Insights as one of the World's Most Valuable Private Unicorns.

https://www.thebrandtechgroup.com

With distributed teams across the US, LATAM, and India, we partner with clients to build high-performance, scalable systems that solve complex technical challenges. Our culture values innovation, ownership, and engineering excellence. We're growing our AI department and are looking for a hands-on AI Developer to help build it.

Role Overview

We are looking for an AI Developer to join and strengthen our AI department. Your core work will be building and operating LLM-powered systems: serving open-source models with Ollama and llama.cpp, building RAG pipelines, and developing MCP integrations that connect large language models to real tools and data. Solid DevOps fundamentals - Docker, CI/CD, Azure - support this work, but AI engineering is the heart of the role.

You don't need to be a deep ML researcher. What matters is production-grade Python, strong fundamentals, and the aptitude to learn fast. You'll work closely with our engineering and product teams to take LLM-powered features from prototype to reliably deployed systems, with mentorship available as you ramp up in areas like RAG architecture, Kafka, and advanced MCP work.

Key Responsibilities

AI / LLM Engineering (core focus)

  • Serve and operate open-source LLMs using Ollama and llama.cpp, locally and in on-prem environments.
  • Build and maintain RAG pipelines: embeddings, vector databases, chunking strategies, and retrieval quality.
  • Develop MCP (Model Context Protocol) integrations connecting LLMs to internal tools and data sources.
  • Build backend services in Python that power ML inference and AI-driven product features.
  • Parse and process structured and semi-structured data (XML/XSD, Office document formats) as pipeline inputs.
  • Grow into model optimization over time: quantization (GGUF), GPU/CUDA tuning, and offline/air-gapped deployments.

DevOps & Infrastructure (supporting)

  • Build and maintain CI/CD pipelines for AI services (Azure DevOps preferred; GitHub Actions / GitLab CI also used).
  • Deploy AI workloads to Microsoft Azure,AWS and containerize services with Docker.
  • Automate operational tasks with Python, Bash and/or PowerShell scripting.
  • Troubleshoot across the stack - dig into root causes rather than patching symptoms.
  • Support event-driven architectures using Apache Kafka (producers/consumers).
  • 3â5+ years engineering experience with production-level Python for building real services, LLM inference, RAG pipelines, and automated tooling.
  • Hands-on LLM & AI integration serving models via Ollama/llama.cpp, implementing vector retrieval/RAG, and developing MCP integrations (GPU/CUDA tuning & model quantization nice to have).
  • Cloud & Infrastructure expertise covering Azure/AWS deployments, Docker containerization, Linux/Windows admin, and CI/CD automation (Azure DevOps, GitHub Actions, or GitLab CI), with Terraform, Kubernetes, Kafka, or systems languages (Go, Rust, C++) as a plus.
  • DevOps, Security & Operations awareness, including Git workflows, scripting (Python, Bash, PowerShell), observability tools (Prometheus/Grafana), DevSecOps, and compliance frameworks (SOC 2, ISO 27001, Zero Trust).
  • Strong problem-solving & communication with a root-cause troubleshooting mindset, self-directed learning, strong ownership, and seamless remote/distributed team collaboration.

jobs.description:
Job Title: Patient Care Advocate 

Job Location: Remote


About Us: 

We are a dedicated team focused on improving access to affordable prescription medications for patients. By partnering with insurance companies, healthcare providers, and pharmacies, we work to reduce the financial burden of medications, ensuring that patients can access the treatments they need without excessive costs. 


Role Overview: 

As a key member of our team, you will help patients navigate our Prescription Payment Plan. This involves working closely with patients, insurance providers, healthcare professionals, and pharmacies to ensure seamless enrollment, eligibility verification, cost-sharing, and prescription fulfillment. 


What You’ll Do: 

  • Patient Enrollment & Eligibility: Assist patients with enrolling in the program, ensuring all necessary personal and insurance information is provided and verifying eligibility. 
  • Prescription Coverage: Help patients confirm that their prescribed medications are covered under the program, and manage the approval process for eligible medications. 
  • Cost-Sharing & Payment: Reduce patients' out-of-pocket costs by applying the program benefits. Manage copayments, coinsurance, and assist with additional copay assistance when applicable. 
  • Prescription Fulfillment: Coordinate with participating pharmacies to ensure the correct application of benefits during prescription filling, ensuring patients pay the reduced amount. 
  • Refills & Continued Use: Support patients by ensuring they continue receiving medications at reduced costs, monitoring adherence to medication regimens, and ensuring continued eligibility. 
  • Program Renewal & Updates: Guide patients through annual renewals and inform them about any updates to the program or medication formulary. 


What We’re Looking For: 

  • High school diploma or GED required
  • Experience in healthcare, insurance or customer service required (experience with prescription assistance programs is a plus)
  • Strong attention to detail and ability to navigate complex processes
  • Excellent communication skills for working with patients, healthcare providers, and pharmacies
  • A genuine passion for helping others and making a positive impact on their healthcare access
  • The ability to work efficiently and collaboratively within a team environment

Success Factors for Working from Home 

  • Private Workspace: A dedicated, quiet workspace with a door that closes, free from ambient noise. 
  • Ergonomics: A comfortable desk and chair setup that allows for the proper installation of necessary equipment. 
  • Reliable Internet Connection: Stable, high-speed internet with a minimum bandwidth of 10 Mbps downstream and 5 Mbps upstream. 
  • Quiet, Distraction-Free Workspace: A dedicated, quiet area where you can focus on delivering excellent customer service without interruptions. 
  • Tech-Savvy: Comfort with technology and ability to learn new systems quickly. 
  • Self-motivation & Independence: Ability to stay productive and manage your time effectively in a remote environment. 
  • Communication Skills: Strong verbal and written communication skills, especially in a virtual setting. 
  • Adaptability: Ability to adapt to changing technologies and procedures while working remotely. 


Compensation & Perks 

  • Hourly Pay: $16.50 per hour 
  • Company-Provided Equipment: All necessary equipment will be provided. 
  • Comprehensive Benefits: Full health insurance package including medical, dental, and vision coverage. 
  • Cell Phone Benefits: $25/month per line for unlimited phone, text, and data (restrictions may apply). 
  • Generous Referral Program: Earn $50 per paycheck for every person you refer—and your referral earns it too! No limits on payouts. 
  • Comprehensive Training: Paid training to ensure you are fully prepared for success. 
  • Career Growth: Opportunities for career advancement and professional development within a leading healthcare provider. 
  • Work-from-Home Convenience: Save time, and money, and reduce your environmental footprint. 
  • Inclusive Culture: We are an Equal Opportunity Employer, including individuals with disabilities and veterans. 

What Success Looks Like: 

  • Reduced out-of-pocket costs for patients through effective cost-sharing and copay assistance 
  • Timely and accurate processing of prescription claims and approvals 
  • High patient satisfaction with the program’s support and streamlined experience 
  • Compliance with program requirements and monitoring of patient eligibility for ongoing assistance 

Why Join Us? 

  • Be part of a team that makes a real difference in patients' lives by reducing the cost of necessary medications 
  • Opportunity for professional growth in the healthcare and insurance sectors 
  • Competitive compensation and benefits package 
  • A collaborative, supportive, and innovative work culture 

Ready to Make an Impact? 

Join us in making prescription medications more affordable and accessible for those who need them most. If you're ready to help make a difference, we'd love to hear from you! 

If you like wild growth and working with happy, enthusiastic over-achievers, you'll enjoy your career with us!

jobs.title: Agile Program Manager
jobs.description:
We're looking for an experienced Agile Program Manager to lead delivery across multiple cross-functional teams working toward a shared set of business outcomes. You'll sit at the intersection of strategy and execution: translating roadmap priorities into coordinated, predictable delivery, keeping dependencies visible, and making sure the right people are making the right decisions at the right time.

This is a hands-on program role, not a status-reporting one. You'll own the cadence, the plan, and the risks across several Agile teams, and you'll be the person stakeholders trust to tell them where things really stand.

What You'll Do

  • Lead end-to-end delivery of a multi-team program, coordinating three or more Agile teams (Scrum, Kanban, or hybrid) toward shared quarterly objectives.
  • Run program-level planning, including quarterly/PI planning, roadmap alignment, capacity planning, and release planning.
  • Identify, map, and actively manage cross-team dependencies, risks, and blockers, escalating early and with clear options.
  • Facilitate program ceremonies such as Scrum of Scrums, program syncs, system demos, and retrospectives, and make sure they produce decisions, not just updates.
  • Partner with Product Owners and Product Managers to keep backlogs prioritized, refined, and aligned to business value.
  • Build and maintain program-level reporting: delivery health, burn-up/velocity trends, OKR or objective progress, and RAID logs, tailored for both team-level and executive audiences.
  • Drive continuous improvement in delivery practices, tooling, and team workflows, coaching teams and leaders on Agile principles where needed.
  • Manage stakeholder communication across engineering, product, design, business, and leadership, keeping expectations aligned as scope and priorities shift.
  • Track program budget, resourcing, and vendor or third-party deliverables where applicable.

What You Bring

  • 8+ years of experience in program or project management, with at least 5 years leading delivery in Agile environments.
  • Proven track record managing multi-team programs (not just single-team Scrum) from planning through release.
  • Deep, practical knowledge of Scrum and Kanban, plus experience with at least one scaling framework (SAFe, LeSS, Scrum@Scale, or similar).
  • Strong command of Agile tooling such as Jira, Jira Align, Azure DevOps, Rally, or equivalent, including building dashboards and program-level reporting.
  • Excellent facilitation skills: you can run a 50-person planning event as comfortably as a tense 1:1 escalation.
  • Clear, concise written and verbal communication in English, with the ability to tailor the message for engineers and executives alike.
  • Experience working with distributed or remote teams across time zones.
  • Comfort operating with ambiguity: you can stand up structure where there is none and adapt it as the program evolves.

Nice to Have

  • Agile or program management certifications such as SAFe RTE, SAFe SPC, PMI-ACP, PgMP, PMP, CSM/CSP, or ICAgile.
  • Experience with Agile transformations or introducing scaled frameworks into an organization.
  • Background in software, SaaS, data, or digital product delivery.
  • Familiarity with OKRs and value-stream or portfolio management.
  • Experience in regulated industries (financial services, healthcare, insurance, public sector) where Agile delivery coexists with compliance requirements.

ABOUT CIVILGRID

CivilGrid is the trusted civil design platform powering affordable infrastructure renewal and growth. We give utilities, civil engineers, and municipalities a single, collaborative source of truth for what's underground so teams can plan, design, and build faster, smarter, and safer.

Our platform consolidates utility records, geotechnical and environmental data, paving moratoriums, and jurisdictional requirements directly from 3,000+ utilities, agencies, and municipalities with full chain-of-custody documentation. Teams at PG&E, Mark Thomas, and dozens of leading engineering firms use CivilGrid to cut research time by up to 88%, reduce project costs, prevent dig-ins, and accelerate delivery on the projects that keep communities running.

We're a venture-backed Series A startup tackling a $4.7T US infrastructure market that has been underserved by software for decades. Founded by industry insiders, each with 10+ years in utilities and civil engineering, we move fast, ship work that matters, and stay close to the customers and field teams we build for.

WHY THIS ROLE

We're looking for a Security & Infrastructure Engineer to own our security posture and assist in supporting our cloud platform and reliability as we scale into large utilities and civil engineering firms. You'll take over and grow our security program, working across engineering, IT, and leadership. The role is on the Systems team that spans DevOps, SRE, and security. Your focus is security but you will contribute across the team.

This role reports to the Head of Engineering. It is a hybrid role with expectations that you are working from our Boston, MA office at least 3 days per week if hired.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Partner with engineering to embed reliability and security into the SDLC and infrastructure decisions

  • Run our security program: SOC 2 readiness and audits, vendor reviews, access controls, endpoint security, and threat modeling

  • Build and maintain our Trust Center, and lead security reviews with customers

  • Contribute to our AWS environment end to end: VPC architecture, ECS, RDS, secrets management, IAM, networking, and cost optimization

  • Contribute to improving reliability practices: SLOs, observability, alerting, on-call rotation, runbooks, and blameless post-incident reviews

  • The tech:

    • AWS ECS, Postgres on RDS managed with CDK

    • GitHub, Datadog, Slack, Notion, Drata

WHAT YOU'LL BRING

  • Experience running or supporting a SOC 2 program, including evidence collection, control design, and auditor coordination

  • Deep working knowledge of AWS (VPC, ECS, RDS, IAM, Secrets Manager, CloudWatch) and infrastructure-as-code (Terraform, CDK, or equivalent)

  • Experience running vulnerability management, from scanner findings and outside reports to fixes shipped

jobs.description:

Application deadline: 16 Nov 2026 23:59 CET

About Claims

AI ate the Internet, but it can't digest science yet. A paper is thousands of words of prose written for humans, but an AI agent doing research needs to know what was claimed, what evidence supports it, and how far to trust it. Claims turns the scientific literature into exactly that: every claim, tied to its evidence, as structured data that models and agents can query.

We're a startup and run as Subnet 111 on Bittensor. Since our mainnet launch on 28 August 2026, an open competition of miners has processed more than 10,000 papers, and every record was checked by our validator before it entered the dataset. The competition keeps raising the bar: miners keep finding ways to beat our own reference pipeline, and every win becomes part of the standard the whole network is scored against.

The team

Claims was founded by two professors of economics and a senior engineer.

  • Philipp Koellinger, CEO, is a professor of economics and an experienced entrepreneur: founder of DeSci Labs and the DeSci Foundation, and co-builder of SciWeave with Ogban.
  • Christian Roessler, co-founder, is a professor of economics and game theorist. He designs the incentive mechanism that makes the miner competition work.
  • Ogban Ugot, engineering, is a senior backend and machine learning engineer. He built SciWeave, the Claims miner, validator and data pipeline, and you will work with him every day.

You would be the fourth person on the team and our second engineer.

Our culture

We are a fully remote team spread across Europe, Africa and the US West Coast. We have a flat hierarchy and move fast towards clearly defined goals. We think deep, don't shy away from difficult problems or conversations, and we ship relentlessly. The code you will write will run on a live network within your first weeks, and you own real things from day one. We are an AI-native company and expect you to be an AI-native Software Engineer we can trust.

About the role

Position: Software Engineer (Python, full-stack)
Location: Remote. You need to be able to join our team meetings in the afternoon, Central European Time.
Type: Full-time contractor. Start in December 2026 or January 2027.

We're looking for a Software Engineer to help maintain and build Claims and its supporting applications, services, and developer tools. Claims turns scientific research into structured claims and supporting evidence through document processing, AI pipelines, and automated evaluation.

This is a hands-on, backend-focused full-stack role. You'll work across Python services, web dashboards, data pipelines, integrations, and deployment tooling. Your work will combine delivering new features with debugging existing systems, improving reliability, and making the codebase easier to maintain.

You should be comfortable owning well-defined tasks from investigation through implementation, testing, and release, working with the team on larger design decisions and unfamiliar areas.

Responsibilities

  • Build and maintain Python backend services, APIs, command-line tools, and background processing workflows.
  • Develop and improve web dashboards and internal review tools using TypeScript, React, and modern web frameworks.
  • Maintain pipelines that ingest research papers, process documents, extract structured information, and evaluate results.
  • Integrate external APIs and AI model providers, handling validation, retries, timeouts, rate limits, and usage costs.
  • Work with relational databases and object storage, including schema changes, migrations, queries, and data integrity checks.
  • Investigate bugs and production issues across services, pipelines, and interfaces; address root causes and add useful regression coverage.
  • Help maintain deployment automation, continuous integration, logging, monitoring, and operational documentation.
  • Improve existing code through practical refactoring, dependency maintenance, automated tests, and code review.
  • Collaborate with engineering and research colleagues to turn requirements and experimental workflows into reliable software.

Required skills and experience

  • Typically 1â5 years of professional software engineering experience, or equivalent practical experience delivering and maintaining production software.
  • Strong Python skills, including building maintainable services or data processing applications, managing dependencies, and writing automated tests.
  • Experience designing, consuming, and troubleshooting HTTP APIs, with a sound understanding of JSON, validation, authentication, and error handling.
  • Working knowledge of TypeScript or JavaScript and experience contributing to React applications or a comparable modern frontend framework.
  • Practical SQL and relational database experience, including data modelling, migrations, and debugging queries.
  • Confidence working in Linux environments and using the command line to investigate logs, configuration, processes, and service failures.
  • Experience with Git, pull requests, code review, automated testing, and continuous integration.
  • An understanding of secure engineering practices, including access controls, secrets management, and careful handling of private data.
  • The ability to navigate an existing codebase, trace issues across components, and make focused, well-tested changes.
  • Clear communication, practical problem-solving, and the judgment to work independently while asking for input when requirements or risks are unclear.

Nice to have

  • Experience with FastAPI, Pydantic, PostgreSQL, Supabase, Next.js, or similar tools.
  • Experience integrating LLM APIs, building AI-assisted workflows, or evaluating model outputs for accuracy, reliability, latency, and cost.
  • Familiarity with PDF parsing, OCR, document extraction, scientific datasets, or evidence provenance.
  • Experience with distributed jobs, asynchronous processing, reproducible pipelines, or automated benchmarking.
  • Familiarity with Docker, Ansible, systemd, GitHub Actions, cloud hosting, or infrastructure automation.
  • Experience with Bittensor, decentralized compute networks, or systems for evaluating independently submitted code.
  • Exposure to Rust, native Python extensions, or WebAssembly.
  • An interest in scientific research, open-source software, and tools that make research easier to inspect and reuse.

You don't need experience with every technology listed. Strong engineering fundamentals and the ability to learn quickly across the stack matter most.

What success looks like

  • You can independently deliver scoped features and fixes across the backend and supporting web applications.
  • Your changes are understandable, tested, and documented, with appropriate attention to security and compatibility.
  • You help make processing pipelines and production services more reliable and easier to troubleshoot.
  • You contribute constructively to reviews, communicate progress and blockers, and help the team turn research ideas into maintainable software.

What we offer

  • $1500 - $2000 per month, depending on experience.
  • Opportunities for rapid professional growth in a high-impact role: a small team, a live network, and a senior engineer to learn from.
  • Quarterly team retreats in inspiring locations (e.g., Vilnius, Koh Samui).
  • Travel and visa support for business needs.
  • Flexible remote working.


Help us build the data layer that lets AI do science properly.

How to apply


Apply online through the link here: https://airtable.com/appZKkV7FT7eYBhKI/shrjJ3jYfxZjsNckR

It takes about 30 minutes: a few practical questions, four short written answers, links to your code, and your CV or personal website. No cover letter needed.

jobs.title: Software Engineer Infrastructure
jobs.description:
Software Engineer, Infrastructure

Hybrid in Palo Alto (Mon / Wed / Thurs) Â· $185Kâ$215K base + meaningful early-stage equity + full benefits

Â 

About Sodalis

Specialty pharmacy is where the most complex and expensive drugs reach the most in-need patients, and it still runs on faxes, phone tag, and manual data entry. Patients wait weeks for therapies that can't wait.

Sodalis is building AI agents that run those operations end to end: reading and validating prescriptions, handling phone calls, and moving prescriptions through eligibility and fulfillment. The ambition goes beyond that. We want to be the rails every specialty prescription runs on, and the first system to perform clinical review at the standard of a pharmacist.

We're already in production, processing tens of thousands of prescriptions a week. Backed by Gradient Ventures (Google's AI fund), and founded by veterans of Apple's Applied ML, Included Health, and Avella Specialty Pharmacy (scaled to $1.5B+ before its acquisition by OptumRx).

Â 

The Opportunity

Everything we run today is cloud-based, and so are the pharmacy management systems we integrate with. But most of the specialty pharmacy market runs on-prem. To reach it, our system has to run on the pharmacy's systems instead of ours. Whether that's the full stack on-site or a hybrid split with our cloud is one of the first decisions you'd make. That's the problem you'd own.
We've never shipped an on-prem deployment, so there's no pattern to follow. You'll decide how our architecture gets packaged and deployed into environments we don't control, what has to change in our current infrastructure to make that possible, and how we maintain and see into those deployments once they're live.

We don't yet know what these environments look like in detail. Some pharmacies may have restricted outbound access, legacy hardware, or IT teams that can't give us a login; others may be more open. Part of the job is going in with our customer, finding out what's actually there, and designing something that works across the range.
You'll start with our AI pharmacy tech product, rolling out with a committed customer, so you build against a real deployment instead of a hypothetical one. You'd work directly with the founders and the early engineering team on the architecture.

What you'll do

  • Decide how our architecture runs in a pharmacy's environment, starting with the AI pharmacy tech product: full stack on-site, a hybrid split with our cloud, or something in between.

  • Adapt our current infrastructure and build the packaging and deployment path that installs and updates Sodalis at each pharmacy.

  • Own those deployments over time: upgrades, rollbacks, and observability into health and failures without being on site.

  • Go in with our customer and pharmacy IT teams to learn what their environments actually allow, and design for the range.

  • Partner with the founders and early engineering team on architecture.

What we're looking for

  • 5+ years in infrastructure or platform engineering.

  • You've taken an AWS-native stack and made it run on Kubernetes or similar in environments you don't operate, including stateful services.

  • You've shipped and maintained software running in environments you don't control: on-prem, customer-hosted, edge, or embedded.

  • You've kept a fleet of remote installs updated, observable, and recoverable without being able to log into them.

  • You've set the first pattern for something in a startup and are comfortable with ambiguity.

  • You'll spend time with pharmacy IT teams and need to understand their constraints firsthand. No healthcare background required.

How we work

We're a handful of people going all in on a problem we think is worth it, holding a high bar and shipping work that reaches real patients. It's intense, and it isn't for everyone. We want people who want to build something that matters, alongside others who care as much as they do. If that's you, we should talk.

We design and operate global systems for data capture, data labeling, and hardware-enabled workflows used by leading AI labs and robotics companies to train and validate humanoid and embodied AI systems.
We work closely with frontier robotics teams to bridge real-world data, simulation, learning-based systems, and deployed hardware.

About the Role

Signing a capture partner is the start of the work. Getting that partner to steady, high-quality output takes onboarding, training, hardware, support, and reporting, and every step has to run on time.

As Partnership Operations Manager, you will own that path for our regional partnership leads so they can focus on finding and signing partners. This is a new function, so you will set the standards and tooling yourself and make them repeatable across regions.

What You Will Do

  • Deal support: Prepare proposals and agreements from approved templates and keep a clean record of every partnerâs rates, volumes, and term dates.

  • Onboarding: Set partners up on the platform, issue devices and accounts, and train their teams on capture standards so they reach full output quickly.

  • Hardware: Manage device allocation, tracking, replacements, and returns with our hardware and logistics teams, and keep inventory records accurate.

  • Partner support: Be the first point of contact for partners, and run the support channel to clear service levels. Resolve problems yourself or route them to product, engineering, or finance before capture is disrupted, and pass on what partners need from the platform and devices.

  • Performance and reporting: Monitor daily performance and quality across partners, including recorded, approved, and deliverable hours, recording counts, and QA rejection rates. Act when numbers slip, and raise anything commercial with the partnerâs regional lead. Keep scorecards, business reviews, and the data behind them current.

  • Payments: Own partner payments and reconciliation, making sure hours are approved correctly and paid accurately and on time.
